vars.name: R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
vars.purpose: R2 S3 secret

vars.name: R2_BUCKET
vars.purpose: private bucket

vars.name: SPACES_ENDPOINT
vars.purpose: DigitalOcean Spaces endpoint

vars.name: SPACES_REGION
vars.purpose: Spaces region

vars.name: SPACES_ACCESS_KEY_ID
vars.purpose: Spaces key

vars.name: SPACES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
vars.purpose: Spaces secret

vars.name: SPACES_BUCKET
vars.purpose: private bucket

vars.name: SCREENING_PROVIDER
vars.purpose: which screening adapter (stand-in in tests)

vars.name: SCREENING_API_KEY
vars.purpose: screening provider auth

vars.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
vars.purpose: Anthropic API (owner key)

vars.name: ANTHROPIC_MODEL
vars.purpose: model id used for writing

vars.name: RENDER_CONCURRENCY
vars.purpose: how many videos one process renders at once (a real render needs about 1.5 GB). Not written down: 1 with the real recorder, 2 with the stand-in

vars.name: RENDER_WEB_ORIGIN
vars.purpose: R6: the web address the video maker opens to play a wish (its /render page and /render-clock.js). Without it the video maker is off and the top tickets stay unsold

vars.name: RENDER_TOKEN_SECRET
vars.purpose: R6: the secret that hashes the one-use token the video maker reads a wish with (32 characters or more). The video maker is off without it

vars.name: RENDER_CHROMIUM_PATH
vars.purpose: R6: the browser program the video maker starts to play a wish

vars.name: RENDER_FFMPEG_PATH
vars.purpose: R6: the ffmpeg program the video maker encodes with (ffprobe is looked up beside it)

vars.name: RENDER_ADAPTER
vars.purpose: R6: `chromium` binds the real video maker even with PROVIDERS=standin (proofs on a machine with other providers on stand-ins). With PROVIDERS=live the real video maker is always chosen when it can work, and this name changes nothing (boot says so in the log)

vars.name: RENDER_STORAGE_HOSTS
vars.purpose: R6: extra storage host names (comma list) the video maker's browser may reach to load the wish's pictures; the storage endpoint already named is added by itself

vars.name: RENDER_ALLOWED_HOSTS
vars.purpose: R6: replaces the video maker browser's whole host list (comma list, host or host:port). Leave out: the web, the API, the storage hosts and the font hosts are allowed

vars.name: RENDER_CLOCK_PATH
vars.purpose: R6: a file holding the stepped clock's page script, read instead of the web's /render-clock.js (tests and proofs only)

vars.name: RENDER_CLOCK_SHA256
vars.purpose: R6: when set, the clock script the web serves must hash to this (hex sha256) or no video is recorded

vars.name: PROCESS_ROLE
vars.purpose: R6: `all` (default: serves requests, runs every job, renders), `web` (serves requests and runs every job but renders; takes no render job) or `render-worker` (takes only render jobs; serves only a health address; `npm run start:render-worker`)

vars.name: RENDER_WORKER_PORT
vars.purpose: R6: the health address port of a render-worker process (bound to 127.0.0.1)

vars.name: RENDER_WORKER_ID
vars.purpose: R6: a name for this machine's render worker, one value per machine and different on every machine (never the hostname of a cloned one). A restarted worker frees the renders it held at once only when this is set and matches; with none set, a render left by a dead worker is freed only when its lease runs out

vars.name: RENDER_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS
vars.purpose: R6: the longest one video render may run, in seconds; the render's lease is longer than this and is renewed while frames still come

vars.name: RENDER_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS
vars.purpose: R6: how long a render token lives, in seconds

vars.name: RESEND_API_KEY
vars.purpose: Resend API auth (R12)

vars.name: RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET
vars.purpose: signing secret of Resend's webhook stream: delivery news and received mail (YY3)

vars.name: MAIL_FROM
vars.purpose: sender address for every email (R12)

vars.name: NODE_ENV
vars.purpose: process mode: development, test or production

vars.name: PORT
vars.purpose: HTTP port

vars.name: PROVIDERS
vars.purpose: live uses real providers; standin uses in-process stand-ins (refused when NODE_ENV=production)

vars.name: STANDIN_MAIL_OUTBOX
vars.purpose: HK1: a file the stand-in email appends each message to, one JSON line (to, template, subject, text, at); tests only, refused with PROVIDERS=live or NODE_ENV=production

vars.name: STANDIN_CLOCK_OFFSET
vars.purpose: HP6: whole seconds added to the stand-in clock, read once at boot; tests and verifier stacks only, refused with PROVIDERS=live or NODE_ENV=production

vars.name: STANDIN_SCREENING
vars.purpose: API-BASE-12 case 4: rules for the stand-in screening by file name, as a comma list of hold:<part of a name> (the file waits in screening) or reject:<part of a name> (the file is refused); tests and verifier stacks only, refused with PROVIDERS=live or NODE_ENV=production

vars.name: STANDIN_VIDEO
vars.purpose: IK3: `fail` makes the stand-in video renderer fail every job; IK7: `hold` makes it wait until the job's token is read (PROVIDERS=standin binds the stand-in renderer, a small marked file); tests and verifier stacks only, refused with PROVIDERS=live or NODE_ENV=production

vars.name: STANDIN_RENDER_TOKENS
vars.purpose: IK7: a file the stand-in video renderer appends each render's one-use token to (mode 0600); test stacks only, refused with PROVIDERS=live or NODE_ENV=production

vars.name: STANDIN_RENDER_HOLD_FILE
vars.purpose: IK7a: with STANDIN_VIDEO=hold, a render holds only if this file exists when the render starts; test stacks only, refused with PROVIDERS=live or NODE_ENV=production

vars.name: RENDER_STANDIN_HOLD_SECONDS
vars.purpose: IK7: the most seconds the stand-in video renderer waits with STANDIN_VIDEO=hold; test stacks only

vars.name: STANDIN_STORAGE_DIR
vars.purpose: R6: a folder that holds the stand-in storage in files, so the web process and the render worker of one test stack see the same files (the stand-in keeps them in memory otherwise); proofs and test stacks only, refused with PROVIDERS=live or NODE_ENV=production

vars.name: INTERNAL_TOKEN
vars.purpose: shared secret an internal route needs in the x-internal-token header (32 or more characters)

vars.name: TRUST_PROXY_HOPS
vars.purpose: proxies in front of the API trusted for the client address (V4); 0 reads the socket address, 1 behind one load balancer. Behind a load balancer set it to 1 (the number of proxies): at 0 every caller seems to come from the balancer's own address, so one flood of wrong guesses at the public link or the render page would be counted against everyone, the video maker included. A render read by a right token has its own limit and does not depend on it

vars.name: PORT_TIMEOUTS_MS
vars.purpose: time limit of one call to a provider port, as port=milliseconds pairs (FF1); payments 10000 unless changed

vars.name: JSON_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES
vars.purpose: the largest JSON body the API reads, in bytes (JJ1); 512 KB, above the 256 KB wish content limit so an oversize wish gets the service's 422
